title: V1 vs V2 at a glance
lead: The two models on the 71 held-out phrases (songs never seen in training), synthesised in one step from the true phoneme durations and F0 and measured with tools/eval_ab.py. Ratios are generated / recording, so 1 means "like the recording"; per-band values are 68 Hz–945 Hz / 973 Hz–2.4 kHz / 2.5–6.1 kHz / 6.3–15.5 kHz. Bold = closer to the recording (ratios closer to 1, offsets closer to 0, error lower).

rows.metric: Spectral-shape peaks and valleys, consonants (per band)
Spectral-shape peaks and valleys, vowels (per band)
Motion at the phoneme rate, 30–150 ms, vowels (per band)
Harmonic peak roughness, < 1 kHz / 1–3 kHz (above 1 = jagged)
Harmonic valley level vs recording (+ = valleys filled in)
Mel error against each model's own training target (non-silent frames)
The same after smoothing both by 21 frames × 21 bins (coarse shape only)

notes: V2 keeps the detail that averaging tends to lose — fine time texture, the spectral shape of consonants, phoneme-rate motion — its harmonic lines are cleaner, and the regular pattern the GAN left is gone.

V2 is not better everywhere: the plain mel error is 0.24 dB higher (the excess is random detail that does not coincide with the recording — smoothing both sides reverses the order, and the phrase-level level is closer for V2); the first and last 20 ms of phonemes are 0.13 dB worse, and the (rare) devoiced vowels are clearly worse (error 7.8 → 11.2 dB, spectral centroid 1.3 kHz low).
One checkpoint each; V1's target is the raw mel, V2's the loudness-corrected mel (the ratio metrics do not depend on the target's level).
